themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 500% spike (z-score: 3.54)—suggesting either a sudden increase in unlicensed or non-compliant vendors in Sunnyside/Woodside or a coordinated enforcement/complaint effort.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Statistically significant anomaly indicating either new vendor activity or complaint surge
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and DCA enforcement to understand what triggered the spike this week
Check if there's a specific location (Astoria Blvd, Queens Blvd, park) seeing concentrated vendor activity

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints doubled to 17 this past week from an 8-week average of 8.0 complaints per week (112% spike, z-score: 3.53), potentially affecting pedestrian safety and evening visibility across the district.
evidence: 17 street light complaints filed last week vs. 8.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (112% spike, z-score 3.53)
Systemic infrastructure failure pattern emerging in high-density commercial/residential corridors
Overlaps with plumbing spike (19 complaints, 127% increase), suggesting possible contractor or utility work disruption
reporting_angles: Map the street light outages geographically—are they concentrated in a corridor or scattered?
Contact Con Edison and DOE to determine if this is weather-related, maintenance backlog, or construction-related damage

themes_detail.label: Plumbing System Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints nearly doubled to 19 last week from an 8-week baseline of 8.4 per week (127% spike, z-score: 4.02), suggesting water infrastructure stress or widespread aging pipe failures in residential and commercial buildings.
evidence: 19 plumbing complaints filed last week vs. 8.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (127% spike, z-score 4.02)
Complements existing 748 heat/hot water complaints (90-day total), indicating broader utility/infrastructure strain
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' suggesting chronic water system underinvestment
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents in older buildings (particularly pre-1980 stock in Woodside/Sunnyside core) about burst pipes, water shutoffs, backups
Consult DEP data on main breaks and aging infrastructure in this specific CD; compare to citywide rates
Investigate whether recent street work (utility trenching, construction permits = 668 filings) has damaged residential service lines

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Branches Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 6 last week from a baseline of 1.8 per week over 8 weeks (243% spike, z-score: 5.13), indicating possible Parks Department maintenance backlog or storm damage.
evidence: 6 overgrown tree/branch complaints filed last week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% spike, z-score 5.13)
Dead animal complaints also spiked 264% last week (5 vs. 1.4 avg), potentially indicating storm damage or ecological stress
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for park/green space expansion, suggesting chronic understaffing of Parks maintenance
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about staffing levels and whether recent weather (high winds, rain) caused branch failures
Map complaint locations to identify which parks or street segments are most affected
Check if this correlates with the 'Walk to Park Site Selection' ULURP project in Queens CD 2 (suggesting park access/quality concerns)

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Reports Spike Sharply
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints surged dramatically 2 weeks ago to 5 complaints versus a baseline of 0.8 per week over 8 weeks (567% spike, z-score: 6.43—highest z-score in dataset), suggesting either a specific dog pack problem or a concentrated neighborhood enforcement/complaint wave.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike, z-score 6.43—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Pattern may indicate a specific location (park, school, transit hub) or recurring dogs creating public safety concern
No recent Reddit discussions or news coverage identifying the source, suggesting under-reported or hyperlocal issue
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 5 complaints from 2 weeks ago to identify if they cluster at a specific park (Sunnyside Park, Astoria Park overspill) or street
Interview NYPD Animal Care and Control about enforcement responses and whether there's a known dog pack or owner creating repeat incidents
Talk to residents near the cluster zone about safety concerns and whether off-leash enforcement is inadequate
